defects.description: Instructions say rest a hand on the raised ankle (hand low, near ankle) and keep torso lifted. PR-v4 auto-fix raised BOTH shoulders to -110 (raw) producing derived shoulder_abduction 134/133 deg — BOTH arms fully overhead. This is the OPPOSITE of hand on ankle. Original pre-PR-v4 values were leftShoulder -20, rightShoulder -32 (per source comment) producing moderate ~40-54 deg abduction (arms at sides, hands near thighs/ankle). PR-v4 overshot the too-subtle fix by 5x.

Instructions say cross one ankle over the opposite knee into a figure-four shape. Derived hip_abduction_deg = 0 for both legs (no spread), knees 95/60 (asymmetric bend but no crossing geometry). No figure-four approximation present. Renderer does not model hip external rotation, but hipAbductR positive can approximate the crossed-leg outward spread.

regression_risk: low-medium - 3-field change. Shoulder revert is well-precedented (returns to documented pre-PR-v4 values). hipAbductR addition is new but small magnitude. Forearm direction may shift slightly due to abduction change.
rationale: Revert shoulders to pre-PR-v4 values (-20, -32) which produced moderate ~40-54 deg abduction (arms at sides with hands near lap, compatible with hand-on-ankle). PR-v4 -110 overshot. Add hipAbductR: 35 (raw positive = leg spreads outward per FK) to approximate figure-four: right leg spreads out so right ankle can cross over left knee. Renderer lacks hip external rotation joint so true figure-four crossing cannot be modeled; abduction is the available approximation. leftKnee 95 stays (supporting foot flat, right angle), rightKnee 60 stays (crossed leg, slight bend). Confidence moderate because hand-on-ankle precise contact cannot be verified without hand position derivation.
